meta.title: Player dossier
meta.honesty: Selections come from published match-day 23s. Points and tries come from the Test score sheets in data/all-blacks-2026.json. Injuries come from All Blacks, RNZ, ESPN and Planet Rugby. Nothing on this page is a rating, a prediction, or a guess at minutes.
meta.checked: On 7 October 2026 the Rugby Database games list and the ESPN New Zealand results page still ended at Baltimore on 12 September. Scores on the seven Tests still agree. The Bledisloe Tests on 10 and 17 October had not been played. No new result was added to the season file.

learnings.title: Ellis Park is the pattern that worked against this Springboks side
learnings.text: The only win of the series was 33–16 at Emirates Airline Park on 22 August. New Zealand scored five tries to one: Will Jordan two, Josh Moorby, Fabian Holland and Luke Jacobson. Ruben Love kicked four conversions and no penalties. Half-time was 12–13, so the lead was built after the break. The All Blacks site, reviewing the series, said the attack can trouble the Springboks. This is the match that showed it. It is also the last Test the side won.

learnings.title: Points took too long, and South Africa punished the mistakes
learnings.text: The All Blacks site said the attack can trouble the Springboks, but New Zealand too often needed long passages of possession to score. In Baltimore, Will Jordan's try finished a patient 32-phase attack. The same report said South Africa were more ruthless after penalties and turnovers. Cape Town was 14–24 at half-time and finished 26–33. Soweto was 12–12 at half-time and finished 24–29, with a penalty try to South Africa. Baltimore finished 28–43. The series was lost 1–3 after the Ellis Park win.

learnings.title: Needless penalties are the points the forwards can stop giving away
learnings.text: After Baltimore, Dave Rennie said needless penalties have to come out of the game, and he called that sort of penalty dumb. The All Blacks site said South Africa were more clinical with the chances they created, especially after penalties and turnovers. The Soweto score sheet includes a penalty try to South Africa. That is seven points with no kicker. ESPN's series review counted 14 scrum penalties conceded, including one penalty try, and a lineout at 86 percent after eight lost throws. Those series counts are ESPN's. They are not re-counted from a second feed here.

learnings.title: The Baltimore set piece was the one Rennie was happy with. The series was not that consistent.
learnings.text: Rennie said the scrum and lineout in Baltimore were excellent. Across the series, the All Blacks site still named set-piece consistency as a review area. Use Baltimore as the picture of the set piece they want, and the ESPN penalty count above as the picture of what leaked in the other Tests. Do not treat the ESPN count as an official All Blacks statistic.

learnings.title: The loose-forward meeting is about replacing Savea and Jacobson, not about a new system
learnings.text: Savea started the first six Tests at No. 8 and captained them. He scored once at Cape Town and twice at Soweto before leaving the field. Jacobson started all six of those Tests at openside and scored at Ellis Park. Both are out of the Bledisloe squad. The loose forwards named on 29 September are Simon Parker, Shannon Frizell, Anton Segner, Ethan Blackadder, Peter Lakai and Wallace Sititi. Frizell has no 2026 Test in these sheets. Rennie said Savea is hard to replace, and that the gap is a chance to give other players time. Codie Taylor is the captain for these two Tests.

learnings.title: The high ball is still the back-three review
learnings.text: After Baltimore, Rennie said the high ball put the side under more heat and that they could not take a lot of those balls. The All Blacks site listed collection of contested kicks as a review area. ESPN wrote that Will Jordan had a series-high 24 high-ball turnovers. That 24 is ESPN's count. It is not on the score sheets and it is not re-counted here. The cue for the back three is the contested kick, not a new attacking shape.

learnings.title: Smaller wingers defending in midfield were moved off the ball
learnings.text: ESPN's series review said Leroy Carter and Josh Moorby, stationed in midfield, were pushed off the ball and that this led to three tries. Both are in the Bledisloe squad. Caleb Clarke, the power wing, is out with a shoulder tendon injury. The meeting point is a defensive one: if Carter or Moorby is in the 13 channel, the collision beside him has to be planned. The three tries are ESPN's reading of the series. They are not listed try-by-try on this page.

learnings.title: First five for the Bledisloe is Mo'unga and Jacomb, with Barrett and McKenzie still in the squad
learnings.text: Ruben Love started the first six Tests at first five and is out for the rest of the season. Richie Mo'unga started Baltimore, his first Test since the 2023 World Cup final. The 29 September squad names Mo'unga and Josh Jacomb as the first fives. Jacomb is uncapped. Beauden Barrett and Damian McKenzie are in the outside backs. Barrett's only Test 23 this year is the Baltimore bench, where he scored. McKenzie started all seven Tests at fullback. Rennie said in September he was happy with Barrett off the bench in Baltimore, and on 4 October he said he expects to use Barrett more at fullback. There is no published match-day 23 for Eden Park yet.

learnings.title: Counter-attack was the plan in July. These sheets do not show whether the tries came that way.
learnings.text: Before the July Tests, Rennie said he treats counter-attack as a set piece because so much possession arrives from kicks, and that he wanted more tries from counter-attack and turnover ball than the year before. The score sheets list who scored. They do not list the phase. So the plan is on the record, and the 35 Test tries are on the record. How many of those 35 started from a kick return is not verified.

learnings.title: The July block was three wins. It is not a six-from-six season.
learnings.text: France 34–32, Italy 47–17, Ireland 40–21, then the Ellis Park win, then three losses. The four tour matches were also wins, and they are not Tests. Their try scorers are not in this file. The mockup that said six from six, and that the Ellis Park Test was still to come, is out of date. Do not brief the team on that record.
